text: Given valid Nutanix credential headers, When an MCP client calls initialize then tools/list, Then the full nutanix_* tool set is returned with descriptions and typed parameters, without any call to Prism Central.

Given one or more of X-Nutanix-Host / X-Nutanix-Username / X-Nutanix-Password is missing, When any tool is called, Then the server returns 401 naming the missing header(s) and makes no request to Prism Central.

Given valid credentials and a mocked Prism Central, When nutanix_list_vms is called with no arguments, Then it returns up to 50 mapped VM records (uuid, name, power_state, cluster) and has_more is set correctly.
Given valid credentials for a real, reachable Prism Central, When nutanix_list_vms is called, Then it returns the cluster's actual VM data.
steps: Obtain a real Prism Central host + a read-capable account
Call nutanix_list_vms with those credentials in the headers
Compare the returned items against the VM list shown in the Prism Central UI for the same cluster
expect: Returned VM names/uuids/power_state match what Prism Central shows for the same cluster
notes: needs a real vendor account / live Prism Central instance -- not available in this pipeline's environment; not executed, not counted as a failure

text: Given a valid VM UUID and a mocked Prism Central, When nutanix_power_vm is called with action=reboot, Then the tool returns the Nutanix task UUID from the triggered operation.
Given a VM UUID that does not exist on the cluster, When nutanix_power_vm is called, Then the tool returns a structured not_found error, not a 500 or an unhandled exception.
Given a mocked Prism Central returns a 5xx or times out, When any tool is called, Then the tool returns {"error":{"code":"upstream_error","retryable":true}}.
Given a mocked Prism Central returns 401/403 (bad credentials), When any tool is called, Then the tool returns {"error":{"code":"unauthorized","retryable":false}}.

Given two concurrent requests carry different X-Nutanix-Host/credential headers, When tools are invoked concurrently, Then neither request's credentials or client/results are observable from the other's context.

Given a real on-prem Prism Central with a self-signed certificate, When a tool connects without X-Nutanix-Verify-Ssl set, Then the TLS failure is reported as a clear upstream_error; When X-Nutanix-Verify-Ssl=false is set, Then the connection succeeds.
steps: Obtain a real on-prem Prism Central known to present a self-signed certificate
Call any read tool without the X-Nutanix-Verify-Ssl header
Call the same tool with X-Nutanix-Verify-Ssl: false
expect: First call returns a clear upstream_error (not a hang or an unhandled exception); second call succeeds and returns data
notes: needs a real vendor account / on-prem Prism Central with a self-signed certificate -- not available in this pipeline's environment; a mock server trivially has a trusted certificate so this cannot be meaningfully simulated

text: Given a list tool is called with limit=1000, Then the effective limit is capped at 200; given no limit is passed, Then the effective limit defaults to 50.
Given /health is called without any Nutanix credentials, Then it returns 200 {"status":"ok"} without attempting to contact Prism Central.
